findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Specify what the printed copy contains, e.g. "a printed copy of the current stipend budget."
findings.violation: "a printed copy" has no clear antecedent - it's never stated what document (the budget? the catalog?) staff would be requesting a copy of.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock being referenced, e.g. "the 90-day service requirement resumes counting on their first day back."
findings.violation: "stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the one-claim-per-benefit-year limit, or something else.

findings.evidence: "eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time"
findings.fix: Identify the reviewer explicitly, e.g. "the benefits team representative checks."
findings.violation: "the reviewer" is introduced with no definition - no prior section establishes who performs this review (manager, benefits team, finance office are all candidates mentioned elsewhere).

findings.evidence: "eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details" (compare to section heading and earlier text: "home-office equipment stipend")
findings.fix: Use a single consistent name for the stipend throughout, or explicitly state that "workspace stipend" and "home-office equipment stipend" are the same benefit.
findings.violation: The document switches between "home-office equipment stipend" and "workspace stipend" without clarifying whether these are the same program or two different stipends.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins." vs. "The manager reviews the request within two business days."
findings.fix: Clarify the actual order of operations, e.g. state that the manager's review happens after submission and produces the approval, removing "manager's approval form" from the pre-submission requirements.
findings.location: How to Apply, first paragraph; compare Approval Timeline
findings.violation: The application step requires the manager's approval to already exist before any review begins, but the Approval Timeline section describes the manager's review as the process that produces that approval - the two sections contradict each other on sequencing.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days." ... "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Use consistent units (e.g. "three business days from submission") throughout the timeline.
findings.violation: The timeline mixes "business days" and plain "days" without clarifying whether the three-day reminder uses the same unit, and doesn't state what the three days are counted from.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests." vs. "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: State one consistent documentation requirement and define which cases, if any, need the physical original rather than a photo.
findings.location: Required Documentation, first paragraph; compare How to Apply
findings.violation: How to Apply requires "the original purchase order" and "the receipt" as hard requirements, while Required Documentation says a photo suffices for "most requests" - it's unclear which requests are exceptions or how the two requirements reconcile.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date" to match the document's style.
findings.violation: "shall" is legalistic phrasing that breaks from the plain, direct tone used everywhere else in the document ("employees keep," "employees must submit"), suggesting inconsistent drafting or a pasted-in clause.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount." / "unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.fix: Add the actual stipend dollar amount or per-category caps that the finance office evaluates against.
findings.violation: The section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never actually states what the stipend amount or cap is, leaving the core monetary detail of the policy undefined.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the office explicitly, e.g. "the benefits team may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: "this office" has no antecedent in the sentence or surrounding text, so it's unclear which office (benefits, finance, people operations) performs the photo check.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device"
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences and explicitly state the exception, e.g. "Normally one device per category is allowed. The benefits team may approve a second device per category when fieldwork requires it, subject to the same annual per-category amount."
findings.violation: This single run-on sentence first limits the stipend to "one device per category" and then describes conditions for approving "a second device," without clarifying whether a second device is actually permitted or how that squares with the one-device limit.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. ... You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g. "The employee records the stipend item on the request form... and tracks its status there."
findings.violation: This section switches to second-person "you," inconsistent with the third-person voice ("employees," "the manager," "the applicant") used throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Align the step list with the full process described in How to Apply, or reference that section instead of restating an incomplete version.
findings.violation: This two-step summary omits steps that How to Apply states are required (manager's approval form, purchase order, reviewing the confirmation summary), so the two sections describe inconsistent processes.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Either remove this duplicated text or replace it with content that actually addresses special-case scenarios, and resolve who (finance liaison vs. benefits team) owns the budget review.
findings.violation: This section is headed "Special Cases" but its content is a near-verbatim duplicate of the Program Overview's budget-tracking text, now attributing the same task to a "finance liaison" instead of "the benefits team," and it never describes any actual special case.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department." (compare Approval Timeline: "The manager reviews the request within two business days.")
findings.fix: Reconcile the two descriptions - state consistently whether the approver is always the employee's manager or varies by department-specific routing.
findings.violation: This section implies the approver varies "based on department," contradicting the Approval Timeline section, which states flatly that "the manager" reviews every request.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what counts as a "repeat request" and describe what the automatic escalation actually does.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" and the escalation process are never defined anywhere else in the document, leaving a core compliance mechanism unexplained.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Replace this section with actual guidance for questions/updates (e.g. a contact point), and resolve the conflicting ownership of budget tracking across the document into a single consistent statement.
findings.violation: This section, headed "Questions and Updates," instead duplicates the Program Overview's catalog/budget text almost verbatim, now attributed to yet a third owner ("people operations office," vs. "benefits team" and "finance liaison" elsewhere), and reuses "entry" language from the equipment-catalog context even though no catalog entries are discussed here.
